name: Systematic listing
definition: Write out the possibilities in an order that guarantees you cannot skip one or write one twice. Alphabetical, smallest first, or by a fixed rule - the order matters less than having one. This is the skill underneath almost every other counting skill.
recognizeWhen: the numbers are small enough to write out
misconceptions: I wrote the possibilities in whatever order they occurred to me and missed some.
I counted the same arrangement twice because I did not recognise it as one I had.
I stopped listing as soon as I had found a few, and assumed that was all of them.
